_readme: Plain-language table. Every entry is verified:false. To mark one verified, read the section in the source and edit the text yourself.

114.title: Return of income
114.plain: Section 114 deals with who must file an income tax return and when. A notice under it asks you to file a missing return.
114.typical_response: File the return through IRIS before the deadline, or write to the office asking for time with a reason.
114.penalty: Late or missing return penalties are in section 182 (see that entry). Exact amounts: UNVERIFIED, check the source.
documents: Salary certificate or income records for the tax year
114.note: Plain-language description written for this tool. Not copied from the legal text. Read the section in the source before relying on it.

114(4).title: Notice to file a return (sub-section 4)
114(4).plain: Under 114(4) the tax office can send a notice asking a person to file a return for one or more past tax years. The text indexed on the FBR site says the notice may cover the last ten completed tax years (check the source).
114(4).typical_response: Reply by filing the return for the named tax year on IRIS before the notice deadline. If you were not required to file, reply in writing with reasons and proof.
114(4).penalty: Not filing can lead to an assessment and penalties (see 182). Amounts UNVERIFIED.
documents: Income records for the named tax year
Proof of any reason you did not need to file
114(4).note: Plain-language description written for this tool. Not copied from the legal text. Read the section in the source before relying on it.

116.title: Wealth statement
116.plain: Section 116 asks for a statement of your assets and liabilities. A notice under it asks you to file or explain it.
116.typical_response: File or correct the wealth statement on IRIS. Keep proof of each asset and loan.
116.note: Plain-language description written for this tool. Not copied from the legal text. Read the section in the source before relying on it.

120.title: Assessment
120.plain: Section 120 covers how a filed return is treated as an assessment. A letter under it usually follows a filed return.
120.typical_response: Read the letter, check the figures against your return, and reply in writing if something is wrong.
120.note: Plain-language description written for this tool. Not copied from the legal text. Read the section in the source before relying on it.

122.title: Amendment of assessment
122.plain: Section 122 lets the tax office change an assessment it thinks is wrong, after giving you a chance to be heard. A notice under it lists what the office thinks is missing.
122.typical_response: Reply in writing by the date given, attach proof for each point, and ask for a hearing. You can also appeal against an order later (section 129). Get advice from a tax professional.
122.penalty: Extra tax and possible penalties. UNVERIFIED, check the source.
documents: Proof for each point in the notice
122.note: Plain-language description written for this tool. Not copied from the legal text. Read the section in the source before relying on it.

129.title: Appeal to the Commissioner (Appeals)
129.plain: Section 129 is the route to appeal against some assessment orders.
129.typical_response: Appeals have time limits and forms. Check the order for the deadline and use IRIS or the office as it directs. Get professional advice.
documents: Proof of payment, if any is required
129.note: Plain-language description written for this tool. Not copied from the legal text. Read the section in the source before relying on it.

161.title: Withholding agent default
161.plain: Section 161 deals with tax that should have been deducted and deposited by a person who pays you or by your business.
161.typical_response: Check what you deducted and deposited. Reply with challans and statements.
161.note: Plain-language description written for this tool. Not copied from the legal text. Read the section in the source before relying on it.

165.title: Statements of withholding
165.plain: Section 165 covers statements of tax deducted that withholding agents must file.
165.typical_response: File the missing statement on IRIS or reply with proof it was filed.
165.note: Plain-language description written for this tool. Not copied from the legal text. Read the section in the source before relying on it.

176.title: Notice to obtain information
176.plain: Section 176 lets the office ask for information or documents.
176.typical_response: Send exactly the items asked for, by the date given, and keep a receipt.
176.note: Plain-language description written for this tool. Not copied from the legal text. Read the section in the source before relying on it.

177.title: Audit
177.plain: Section 177 covers audit. A notice asks you to produce records so the office can check your return.
177.typical_response: Send the requested records by the deadline. If you need time, ask in writing before the deadline.
177.penalty: Not producing the records can lead to a penalty that grows with each notice (see 182). A summary of FBR's section 182 page gave 25,000, 50,000 and 100,000 rupees for the first, second and third failure. That figure is UNVERIFIED, check the source.
documents: Books of account or income records
177.note: Plain-language description written for this tool. Not copied from the legal text. Read the section in the source before relying on it.

182.title: Penalties
182.plain: Section 182 lists penalties for failures such as not filing a return on time or not producing records. A notice under 182 is usually a show-cause: it asks why a penalty should not be imposed.
182.typical_response: Reply before the deadline with the reason for the delay and proof (illness, system problem, or that you already complied). File the missing return or documents too.
182.penalty: A summary of FBR's section 182 page gave, for a late return, 0.1 percent of tax payable per day up to a cap, with a minimum amount. The figures are UNVERIFIED. Read the section in the source.
documents: Proof of the reason for delay
Copy of the return or documents now filed
182.note: Plain-language description written for this tool. Not copied from the legal text. Read the section in the source before relying on it.

140.title: Recovery from third parties
140.plain: Section 140 allows the office to ask a bank or other person holding your money to pay the tax due to the government.
140.typical_response: Check whether the demand is correct. If you disagree, reply in writing straight away and ask a tax professional about a stay.
140.note: Plain-language description written for this tool. Not copied from the legal text. Read the section in the source before relying on it.
